Notes: COMPLETED 2026-09-05. Accept / discard / undo per recommendation plus accept-all, rendered as a git-style diff - struck red for what goes, green for what arrives. Download and screen both read the derived text, so they cannot disagree. Page fit is re-checked on every accept and blocks an overflow. Unapplicable recommendations are rejected at settle time and counted, never dropped silently.

Notes: Raised 2026-09-02. Foundations exist: ai_jobs.usage already records measured tokens per run, and lib/ai/pricing.ts holds the rate tables. MOVED TO PHASE 1.5 2026-09-05 on the owner's instruction. GROUNDING MUST BE TRACKED EXPLICITLY, not folded into token cost: it is billed PER REQUEST, not per token, free to 5,000/month and billed per thousand after. features/ai/cost.ts already counts groundedRuns and computes groundingUsdIfBillable but does NOT add it to totalUsd, because inside the free allowance it genuinely costs zero - so the running total is honest only while the allowance holds. Once month-to-date grounding requests are tracked (this story), the total must switch to billing them above 5,000. Until then the workspace understates cost for any month that crosses the threshold. Pairs with JSV2S1146, which may remove grounding from scoring entirely. PARTIALLY BUILT 2026-09-05: features/ai/grounding.ts (pure) + getGroundingUsage() count month-to-date grounded requests against the 5,000 free allowance and surface a meter in the cost card - used/free, warn at 80%, and the MARGINAL cost of the next request, which is zero inside the allowance and $0.014 outside it. 6 unit tests. STILL OPEN: totalUsd does not yet add billable grounding once the allowance is crossed, and Gemini token spend is not yet aggregated per model. COMPLETED 2026-09-05. The two gaps are closed. (1) BILLABLE GROUNDING IS NOW IN THE TOTAL: billableGroundedRunIds() orders the month's grounded runs by finish time and treats everything past the 5,000th as billed, so billability is a property of a run's POSITION IN THE MONTH rather than of the run - the same application legitimately costs more in a month where it lands past the allowance. Computed once per page and shared by the detail view and the batched list query, so the two can never disagree. A run with no finishedAt sorts last, i.e. billed only if the allowance has already gone - the conservative reading. (2) Gemini token spend per model was already covered by byModel. 10 unit tests. The card now states plainly whether grounding added anything or fell inside the allowance.

Task: [Functional] Capture and measure Apify actor spend alongside AI spend

Notes: Raised 2026-09-05 on the user's instruction. Apify has a defined cost structure, so this is measurable rather than estimated. DESIGN POINT: ingestion cost is per RUN, AI cost is per APPLICATION - a run cost must be amortised across the jobs it yielded, and a night that surfaces 330 jobs of which 14% qualify makes the per-application ingestion cost roughly 7x the per-job cost. Report both, and never fold the two into one number silently. ingestion_runs already exists (migration 0005) and is the right place to stamp the cost. Depends on the Apify decisions in JSV2S1019. 2026-09-05: THE COST MODEL IS NOW KNOWN AND RECORDED in config/apify.ts, read from the actor API rather than the store page: PAY_PER_EVENT on the Free tier, $0.0004 per dataset item ($0.40/1K results) plus $0.001 per actor start, charged once per GB of memory. estimateFetchCostUsd() prices a plan before it runs. NOTE the start charge means a run that returns NOTHING still costs money, so "fetched and found no new jobs" is not free - the run ledger must record cost even for an empty run. Still to build: stamping actual cost onto ingestion_runs and amortising it across the jobs a run produced.

That gap is the primary thing to explain, and it is not a model choice - candidates: the Console applies its own system prompt and harness on top of the skill; extended thinking may be configured differently; sampling defaults differ; a Console conversation carries context the API call does not; and our prompt is a PORT of the skill, not the skill itself - DELIVERY_OVERRIDE, the output contracts and the length budget were all added by us and change the instruction the model actually receives. Diff the exact prompt sent (ai_jobs.prompt stores it verbatim) against the Console skill before concluding anything about the model. Cost work (JSV2S1150) must not start until this baseline exists.

Task: [Functional] Filter the pre-qualification queue by deciding factor and date
Description: Filter the review and rejected queues by which filter drove the verdict and when it was judged, so the gate can be tuned against real volume rather than inspected one job at a time.
Notes: Raised and BUILT 2026-09-17 on the owner's instruction, from the questions "all rejected jobs last week because of experience" and "all review jobs yesterday because of domain". Two dimensions over the existing view: factor (role/domain/experience/location, multi-select, toggling) and window (today/yesterday/last 7/last 30/any). FILTERS ON decidedBy, NOT ON ANY FAILING FILTER - the Axon job failed both domain and experience, but domain decided it; counting it under experience as well would double-count and send tuning after the wrong rule. Per-factor counts are shown beside each chip so an empty facet is visibly empty rather than a dead end, and the empty state distinguishes "nothing matches these filters" from "the queue is clear". State lives entirely in the URL, so a filtered view is linkable and the back button works. "Yesterday" is bounded on BOTH sides - an open-ended lower bound is the commonest way a date filter lies. Window vocabulary lives in lib/config/constants.ts rather than queries.ts, which opens a database connection at import and would break the unit suite.

Description: Stop rejecting jobs whose stated experience minimum is open-ended, and relax the seniority floor when the title itself reads as senior.
Notes: Raised and FIXED 2026-09-17 from a real false negative the owner spotted. The guard read `found.max ?? found.min`, which treated an OPEN-ENDED minimum as a ceiling: "4+ years" has no top, but the fallback made the top 4, and 4 < the 5-year floor failed a nine-year candidate. MEASURED COST across the 95 stored jobs: four rejected outright - a Wise Senior PM role in London and two Ebury payment-screening roles among them - which is 6% of the reject pile, biased toward exactly the employers worth having, because fintechs write "4+ years" far more often than "8-12 years". Only a CLOSED range can indicate a junior role now. Second change, on the owner's instruction: a primary-tier title outranks a low stated minimum, so "Senior Product Manager, 2-4 years" routes to REVIEW rather than reject - relaxed, not blind, and ABOVE_CEILING still fails whatever the title says. Replayed over the stored corpus: 64 rejects -> 60, Wise and both Ebury roles now PASS, 9fin moves to review where domain is its real limiter. Axon stays rejected, correctly. Also corrected the DOMAIN_GATE doc comment, which still described pass:5/review:2 and had been untrue since the gate was lowered on 2026-09-04.
